documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Course Policy
tiers: Option 2: Generative AI Permitted with Specific Limits
Option 3: Generative AI Permitted with Disclosure and Reflection
documents.summary: A university template that instructors adopt in their syllabi. It gives three options (no AI, AI with specific limits, AI with disclosure and reflection) and adds shared responsibilities and Turnitin and process-evidence text for options 2 and 3.
documents.stance_why: The document says 'Choose which option from 1-3 fits your course' and offers named tiers (Not Permitted, Specific Limits, Disclosure and Reflection); it sets no single stance itself, so it delegates.

units.why: Framing sentence says GAI outputs 'may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or misleading'; an informing statement that outputs are fallible, so P31 (AI output is often wrong), actor all, informs.
units.anchor: their outputs may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or misleading
units.frag_start: While they can sometimes be helpful

units.why: States 'You are responsible for demonstrating your own learning'; responsibility for own learning and following integrity, privacy and accessibility policies fits P29 (students own what they submit) better than P30, since no explaining is mentioned.
units.anchor: You are responsible for demonstrating your own learning
units.policy: Students are responsible for demonstrating their own learning and for following university policies on academic integrity, privacy, and accessibility.

units.why: The document says 'Choose which option from 1-3 fits your course', so each instructor picks one of three options; this is the instructor-sets-the-rule type P04. The options themselves are tiers, coded in the next unit as P05.
units.anchor: Choose which option from 1-3 fits your course
units.policy: Instructors choose which of three options fits their course and may update and change specifics as needed.

units.why: Three named options (Not Permitted, Specific Limits, Disclosure and Reflection) are named levels of AI use, so P05; 'Option 2: Generative AI Permitted with Specific Limits' is the most load-bearing label.
units.anchor: Option 2: Generative AI Permitted with Specific Limits
units.policy: The policy offers three named options: Generative AI Not Permitted, Generative AI Permitted with Specific Limits, and Generative AI Permitted with Disclosure and Reflection.

units.why: Option 1 says 'you may not use generative artificial intelligence tools' in the course: a blanket ban, so default prohibition P01, must-not, prohibit.
units.anchor: In this course, you may not use generative artificial intelligence tools.

units.why: Option 1 requires work be created 'without assistance from AI tools for writing, analysis, problem-solving, or content generation'; students may not have AI produce submitted work, so P19 (the general ban is coded separately as P01).
units.anchor: All submitted work must be created by you, without assistance from AI tools

units.why: Option 1 extends the ban to 'AI-generated content created by someone else', i.e. submitting others' AI output as one's own; P19.
units.anchor: submitting AI-generated content created by someone else
units.frag_end: did not personally use the tool.
units.policy: The ban includes submitting AI-generated content created by someone else (such as a friend, tutor, online service, or shared AI output), even if the student did not personally use the tool.

units.why: Rationale for Option 1: skills 'focus on developing independent thinking, foundational skills, and original intellectual work' and 'take time and practice to build'; AI outsourcing undermines practice, so P41 (P42 would need novices specifically, which is not stated).
units.anchor: These skills take time and practice to build
units.frag_start: This policy supports the learning goals
units.policy: The no-AI option supports learning goals focused on independent thinking, foundational skills, and original intellectual work, which take time and practice to build.

units.why: Option 1 says unpermitted use 'is an academic integrity concern and will be addressed in accordance with university procedures', classifying misuse as an integrity matter: P36.
units.anchor: is an academic integrity concern and will be addressed in accordance with university procedures

units.why: 'Approved accommodations that involve assistive technologies are not restricted by this policy' creates an access exception; fits P51 (accommodations and alternatives exist). Repeated verbatim under Options 2 and 3, coded once.
units.anchor: Approved accommodations that involve assistive technologies are not restricted by this policy.

units.why: 'When AI tools are permitted, I expect you to use them thoughtfully and ethically' is a general conduct expectation; no listed type fits (P29 and P32 are about ownership and primary thinking), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: When AI tools are permitted, I expect you to use them thoughtfully and ethically.
units.policy: When AI tools are permitted, instructors expect students to use them thoughtfully and ethically.
units.uncovered_note: General expectation of thoughtful and ethical AI use when permitted, not specific to any listed type.

units.why: Students are 'responsible for submitting work that reflects your own thinking, learning, and effort'; students own submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: responsible for submitting work that reflects your own thinking, learning, and effort
units.frag_start: You are responsible for submitting work

units.why: The list says students should 'Follow the AI guidelines for this course and each assignment'; compliance with per-course and per-assignment rules, which fits P04 (rule set per course or assignment) best.
units.anchor: Follow the AI guidelines for this course and each assignment
units.frag_start: Follow the AI guidelines for this

units.why: 'Disclose any permitted use of generative AI' requires disclosing AI use with submissions: P24.
units.anchor: Disclose any permitted use of generative AI

units.why: 'Check the accuracy of any AI-influenced content' tells students to verify AI output: P31.
units.anchor: Check the accuracy of any AI-influenced content

units.why: 'Make sure your work reflects your understanding' asks students to understand what they submit; closest is P30, though 'explain every line' is not stated.
units.anchor: Make sure your work reflects your understanding

units.why: 'Not submit AI-generated content created by someone else' repeats the Option 1 rule inside the Options 2 and 3 responsibilities list; a separate statement with a separate scope, P19.
units.anchor: Not submit AI-generated content created by someone else

units.why: Instructor is 'responsible for clearly explaining how generative AI may or may not be used in this course'; a duty to communicate expectations, P09.
units.anchor: clearly explaining how generative AI may or may not be used in this course
units.frag_start: I am responsible for clearly explaining
units.policy: Instructors are responsible for clearly explaining how generative AI may or may not be used in the course and for designing assignments that support learning.

units.why: 'Explaining AI expectations in the syllabus and assignments' specifies that expectations go in the syllabus and assignments: P09.
units.anchor: Explaining AI expectations in the syllabus and assignments

units.why: 'Using tools like Turnitin responsibly' is an instructor commitment about detection tools; P40 covers use of similarity and AI-detection tools (P39, not relying on detectors, is not stated).
units.anchor: Using tools like Turnitin responsibly

units.why: 'Looking at context and your explanation if questions arise' commits instructors to consider the student's context before judging suspected misuse, matching P57; chosen over P64 because it stresses gathering context rather than a formal right to respond.
units.anchor: Looking at context and your explanation if questions arise

units.why: Students 'agree to its use' of Turnitin including 'text-matching and AI-related analysis features' by enrolling; an AI-detection and similarity tool is used on submissions: P40.
units.anchor: including text-matching and AI-related analysis features
units.frag_start: Some assignments may be submitted through Turnitin.
units.policy: Some assignments may be submitted through Turnitin, and by enrolling and submitting work students agree to its use under the university's agreement, including text-matching and AI-related analysis features.

units.why: 'I may use Turnitin as one way to review submissions' says the instructor may use it as one means of review, not sole proof; use of a detection tool, P40.
units.anchor: I may use Turnitin as one way to review submissions.

units.why: 'I may ask to see drafts, revision histories, or notes' uses process evidence when suspicion arises; P40 includes histories as evidence, preferred over P26 which is about students keeping and submitting logs up front.
units.anchor: I may ask to see drafts, revision histories, or notes
units.frag_start: If questions come up, I may ask

units.why: Option 2 says 'You may use generative artificial intelligence tools in this course, but only for specific purposes and/or on specific assignments': AI allowed only for narrow uses set by the instructor, restrict; type P04 because the instructor outlines uses per assignment (tiers are P05 above).
units.anchor: only for specific purposes and/or on specific assignments, as outlined by your instructor
units.frag_start: You may use generative artificial intelligence

units.why: Option 2 says tools 'should not replace your own thinking, problem-solving, or writing': students stay primary problem-solvers, P32.
units.anchor: they should not replace your own thinking, problem-solving, or writing
units.frag_start: When used thoughtfully, these tools can

units.why: Suggested permitted use 'Brainstorming ideas or exploring possible approaches' matches P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming ideas or exploring possible approaches

units.why: Suggested permitted use 'Grammar, clarity, or style suggestions' is AI for prose, P18.
units.anchor: Grammar, clarity, or style suggestions

units.why: Suggested permitted use 'Outline development or early planning' is a planning aid, closest to exploring approaches (P15); no better type.
units.anchor: Outline development or early planning

units.why: Suggested prohibited use 'Having AI write full assignments or responses for you' is P19.
units.anchor: Having AI write full assignments or responses for you

units.why: Suggested prohibited use 'Submitting AI-generated content created by someone else' in the Option 2 list; a distinct listed item, P19.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated content created by someone else

units.why: Suggested prohibited use 'Completing graded problem-solving tasks using AI' bars AI from producing graded solutions: P19.
units.anchor: Completing graded problem-solving tasks using AI

units.why: Suggested prohibited use 'Summarizing assigned course readings unless explicitly permitted' bars a study-aid use (summaries) by default; P14 names summaries as its subject, so P14 with a prohibit unit_stance.
units.anchor: Summarizing assigned course readings unless explicitly permitted

units.why: 'All other uses of GAI not specified as permitted or previously discussed with me' are prohibited: a fallback rule for unlisted uses, P06.
units.anchor: All other uses of GAI not specified as permitted or previously discussed with me
units.policy: All other uses of GAI not specified as permitted or previously discussed with the instructor are prohibited.

units.why: 'Submitting work created by someone else or by an AI system as if it were your own work is not allowed': passing off AI work as one's own, P19.
units.anchor: an AI system as if it were your own work is not allowed.

units.why: 'Using generative AI does not shift responsibility away from you. You remain the author of your work' states ownership, P29.
units.anchor: You remain the author of your work.
units.policy: Using generative AI does not shift responsibility away from the student, who remains the author of the work.

units.why: 'you must include a brief disclosure statement with your assignment' requires a statement with each submission when AI is used: P24.
units.anchor: you must include a brief disclosure statement with your assignment
units.frag_start: Any time you use generative AI,

units.why: 'Failure to disclose permitted GAI is an academic integrity violation' makes nondisclosure the violation: P28 (P36 would classify misuse in general; this is specifically about disclosure).
units.anchor: Failure to disclose permitted GAI is an academic integrity violation.

units.why: Students are 'responsible for ensuring that the final work reflects your own understanding, effort, and learning'; ownership of the final submission, P29.
units.anchor: responsible for ensuring that the final work reflects your own understanding, effort, and learning

units.why: Option 3 says 'You may use generative artificial intelligence tools in this course, as long as you are open and transparent': permitted by default with disclosure, P02.
units.anchor: as long as you are open and transparent about how you use them
units.frag_start: You may use generative artificial intelligence

units.why: Option 3 requires a disclosure naming 'Which tool(s) you used', 'How you used the tool' and 'Why you chose to use it'; naming tool and use fits P25 rather than generic P24.
units.anchor: you must include a short disclosure that explains
units.frag_start: If you use GAI at any stage
units.frag_end: Why you chose to use it
units.policy: If a student uses GAI at any stage of their work, they must include a short disclosure that explains which tool(s) they used, how they used the tool, and why they chose to use it.

units.why: Disclosure must also explain 'Any limitations, inaccuracies, or concerns you noticed in the output', a reflection on the AI output: P26.
units.anchor: Any limitations, inaccuracies, or concerns you noticed in the output
units.policy: The disclosure must explain any limitations, inaccuracies, or concerns the student noticed in the AI output.

units.why: 'This disclosure should appear as a clearly labeled section or appendix with your submission' says where the disclosure goes: P24.
units.anchor: clearly labeled section or appendix with your submission
units.policy: The disclosure should appear as a clearly labeled section or appendix with the submission.

units.why: 'You must submit work that reflects your own thinking and learning' under Option 3: ownership, P29.
units.anchor: You must submit work that reflects your own thinking and learning.

units.why: 'presenting AI-generated content as if it were entirely your own, is not permitted even when AI use is allowed': no passing off AI output as own, P19.
units.anchor: entirely your own, is not permitted even when AI use is allowed
units.frag_start: Submitting AI-generated content created by someone
units.frag_end: even when AI use is allowed.

units.why: Option 3 repeats 'Failure to disclose permitted GAI is an academic integrity violation' in its own scope; distinct option, same type P28.
units.anchor: Failure to disclose permitted GAI is an academic integrity violation.

notes: Single university-level template; no school or computing policy found. Responsibilities and Turnitin text is marked in the source as for Options 2 and 3 only.
